_doc: The SA-02m-web-build quality-tools registry (PROTOCOL.md `## Quality tools`). The one home for 'what does GREEN mean for this web project'. Each row is a self-contained check the runner (`.ai-dev/quality/run.mjs <beat>`) executes wholesale for its beat. The Builder runs every `build`-beat tool on completion and hands back only when they pass; the Reviewer confirms the `review`-beat tools ran and reads their output; `ship`-beat tools run before the merge stamp. Adding or changing a tool = a row here + (optionally) its native config beside this file — never a runner edit.

_row_shape.checks: one plain line: what this tool catches
_row_shape.config: path to its native config beside this file, or null if none
_row_shape.run: the command to run it (from the project root — the runner's cwd)
_row_shape.covers: optional array of path prefixes/globs; run.mjs --touched runs a row only when the diff touches a covered path (rows without covers always run)
_row_shape.init: one line: how to install/enable it

tools.checks: Syntax errors in every hand-written frontend script under static/js/ (recursive: the top-level bundles, app/*.js from the F10 decomposition, and any module directory added later — mqtt/, flasher/, ...) — a broken script bricks the whole UI since there is no build step. MODULE-AWARE: a file with a line-leading `import`/`export` is checked via `node --input-type=module --check < file` because plain `node --check` exits 0 on a broken .js ES module (Node 20/24 module-detection — docs/decisions/es-modules.md П1); classic scripts are parsed via `node --input-type=commonjs --check < file` (pinned, not detection-prone: a mid-line `export`/`import.meta` in a file the heuristic calls classic FAILS loudly instead of slipping through). Fail-closed both directions; residual stated in the script header. Non-vacuous: zero files swept = FAIL; the split is pinned by scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh (row js-syntax-gate).
tools.init: Node 18+ + bash

tools.checks: Non-vacuity of the js-syntax row (scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh): re-proves on the local Node that `node --check` passes a broken .js module, then asserts the shipped gate FAILS a broken module and a broken classic script, PASSES valid ones, does not misread the bundles' `exportHistory()`/`exported_at:` lines or a dynamic `import()` as module syntax (a non-strict classic body must not be parsed as a module), closes the false-CLASSIC direction (a broken file whose only ESM marker is a mid-line `export` or `import.meta` still FAILS on the pinned commonjs parse where plain `node --check` passes it), fails a missing file, and sweeps a non-empty tree. Without it the module branch of the gate could silently regress to the pre-fix vacuous pass the day the first ES module lands.
tools.init: bash + Node 18+ (no other deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-js-syntax-gate.sh

tools.checks: Bash syntax errors in every CGI endpoint and shared lib — a broken CGI returns 500 with no client-side trace.
tools.run: bash -c 'set -e; for f in www/network_config/cgi-bin/*.cgi www/network_config/cgi-bin/lib_*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done'

tools.checks: Syntax errors in every Python file this repo ships or runs — on-device services under opt/ (the Modbus-MQTT bridge, snapshot/scan/monitor helpers, the flasher), device helpers under etc/ (sa02m-grat-arp.py has a systemd unit + cron; sa02m-mqtt-external-info.py is installed by scripts/05-mqtt.sh), and the dev/build tooling under scripts/ and tools/ (imaging, ssh, update, version sync). A broken script fails only when systemd starts it on the device — or mid-deploy — and there is no build step to catch it. Audit 2026-08-26 H2: the row covered opt/ ONLY, so a syntax error in the etc/ helpers passed the full build beat.

tools.checks: The Alice in-place reload seam (1.0.6.19), whose failure mode is SILENT: `config_watch` is a string shared across two languages — the Python client writes it into /run/sa02m-alice/status.json, the privileged shell helper reads it to decide whether a binding edit still needs a unit restart. Rename it on one side and the helper restarts forever: safe, but the whole fix is dead and nothing says so. Part A pins statically that config_watch lives on BOTH sides, that the helper's `restart` verb keeps its `systemctl restart` fail-closed fallback, that every systemctl in the helper is timeout-bounded (the CGI calls it synchronously inside nginx's 20 s budget), that the decision ALSO requires state=connected, that the state string matches the client's STATE_CONNECTED, and that STATUS_STALE_S agrees between constants.py and the helper. Part B extracts the SHIPPED alice_reload_capable() and runs it against a sandboxed status file with a scripted systemctl shim over the whole matrix — only connected + fresh flag + active unit reloads; older client / flag false / stale heartbeat / future-dated ts / no ts / unparseable / empty / absent file / inactive unit, AND every non-connected state (missing_cert, error, offline, connecting, disabled, missing_deps, absent state key, a state merely CONTAINING 'connected') ALL fall back to the restart. The state dimension is the one that matters most: config_watch is a static property of the BINARY (written in every state) while the helper needs a property of the PROCESS — without it the skip also silences the complete_link cert nudge, which shares this one verb, leaving the card at «нет сертификата» (review finding 1, 1.0.6.19). That behavioural half is where the genuine regression class lives — the helper skipping a restart it needed to do — which no grep can see. Non-vacuous: fewer than 4 systemctl calls or a failed extraction FAILS; proven RED by 11 mutations (client/helper config_watch rename, deleted restart fallback, unbounded systemctl, STATUS_STALE_S skew, removed freshness checks, neutered liveness check, and four on the state gate: deleted, neutered, loosened to any state, client renames STATE_CONNECTED).
tools.init: bash + grep + sed + mktemp (present everywhere the project builds) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-alice-reload-handshake.sh

tools.checks: Static gate for docs/contracts/ethernet-iface-naming.md: the legacy-name ledger (only the compat layer, the rename script and the installer migration may name end0/end1 — non-vacuous both ways), the installer still installing AND enabling sa02m-iface-canonical.service, the F6 guard (no `echo -e` in apply.cgi and conf writes only through the two known writers), the §5.4 rm-helper pins (no raw `sudo rm` in apply.cgi; the pinned sa02m-conf-rm.sh sudoers grant present), and the contract §1.0/§7 ordering pins: the unit ordered Before=networking.service, After=+Wants= systemd-udevd + systemd-udev-trigger (else the boot-0 pre-udevd no-op returns), NO Wants=systemd-udev-settle (else the 120 s whole-queue stall returns), fix-eth@.service After=networking.service (else the double-ifup 'File exists' race returns), the rename script still gating canonicalize_pair on udev_initialized (else the boot-0 class returns silently), and 02-network.sh writing `source /etc/network/interfaces.d/*.conf` with no unfiltered `*` line (else <conf>.sa02m-bak backups go live: duplicate stanza -> 'File exists' -> networking FAILED, §1.0 mechanism 3).

tools.checks: The escalation-CLOSED gate for audit B1 (web session -> root without the root password): the single-home www-data sudoers grant (etc/sudoers.d/sa02m-www) lists ONLY pinned helpers and fixed argument vectors — no raw tee (arbitrary root file-write), no bare/wildcard ifup/ifdown (root exec via a pre-up stanza), no raw kill, no i2cset/i2cget/gpioset/gpioget at all (I2C via group i2c, GPIO via the pinned helper); apply.cgi carries 0 `sudo tee` and routes both writers through sa02m-iface-conf-write.sh; the two pinned helpers exist and validate (iface-conf-write: 4-name case allow-list + symlink refusal + CONTENT validation — a per-line ifupdown allow-list where exec/hook directives (pre-up/up/post-up/*-down/source/mapping) are permitted ONLY in the enumerated safe forms (klogic adjust hook, installer default-route hook) so www-data cannot plant a root-exec pre-up/post-up hook that `ifup` would run — the B1-round-2 COMPOSITION escalation; usb-power: closed verb set + gpioset-cmdline kill guard); lib_hw holds no raw sudo tee/gpioset/gpioget/kill and no dead sudo i2cset/i2cget fallback; the i2c drop-grant prerequisite lives in the SAME change (both installer paths keep `usermod -aG i2c www-data` and the i2c udev rule is present — drop-grant-without-group = beeper break); and the grant is single-home (both 03-webserver.sh and update-www-only.sh install the committed file wholesale via sa02m_install_sudoers, no heredoc, no append, the .fragment gone — so an installer re-run REMOVES a stale dangerous grant). Plus a sandboxed behavioural run of the SHIPPED iface-conf-write helper (allow-listed name + valid content written from stdin; a non-allow-listed dest refused exit 2; a symlink dest refused exit 2, target untouched; the COMPOSITION case — an allow-listed dest whose CONTENT plants `pre-up /bin/sh …` is REFUSED with no write (RED against a verbatim writer, GREEN against the content validator), a hostile post-up and an unknown keyword refused, while a legitimate static+klogic-hook conf and the installer default-route-hook conf still write) — the escalation-closed + function-preserved proof, sed-retargeted into a temp dir. Non-vacuous: a missing file, a gutted grant, or a dropped pin FAILS. RED against the pre-fix tree (no committed file, raw tee in the 03-webserver heredoc, sudo i2cset in lib_hw), GREEN after. Device-only residual (stated in the check header): the real `sudo -n tee -> refused` needs the sudoers loaded + real sudo; modelled here by the granted-Cmnd assertions, and `visudo -cf` runs on every install via sa02m_harden_sudoers.
tools.init: bash + grep + mktemp (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for docs/contracts/kernel-conditional-services.md: the opcua gateway port default agrees between etc/sa02m-mqtt-opcua.conf and BOTH py defaults and is not 4840 (CODESYS's own OPC UA server owns 4840 — a regression re-creates the EADDRINUSE crash-loop), sa02m-grat-arp@.service stays Type=simple (a oneshot regression re-blocks multi-user.target ~29 s), the kernel-service guard script + unit + docker ExecCondition drop-in exist and 01-system.sh installs/enables them and runs apply-policy, 08-codesys.sh carries no unconditional enable/start of codesyscontrol (install-only policy), service-ctl cmd_start/codesys_install carry no codesys_rc_enable (start = runtime only), the boot-hold pins: sa02m-modem-dhcp@.service stays event-driven (no [Install] — a statically enabled instance holds multi-user ~90 s on an absent modem) with the 99-modem.rules start line and the 01-system.sh stale-symlink cleanup in place, and sa02m-mqtt-opcua.py sends exactly one sd_notify("READY=1") at the top of main() BEFORE `gw = OpcuaGateway(cfg)` (early READY decouples the OPC UA address-space build — ~9 s in OpcuaServer() construction inside __init__, ~17 s total — from multi-user.target; moving it into/after construction reintroduces the boot hold, contract §5.1). Non-vacuous: a missing file or an empty extraction FAILS.
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for the hardware watchdog policy homed in etc/systemd/sa02m-watchdog.conf. Cap pin (open-world): it SWEEPS etc/ scripts/ tools/ opt/ www/ install.sh, so a brand-new writer is judged too, not just the enumerated copies — every RuntimeWatchdogSec/RebootWatchdogSec/ShutdownWatchdogSec value parses to <=16s (the sun4i-wdt cap on the A40i) or is an explicit disable, with durations NORMALISED first: a naive compare reads the original defect's `2min` as 2, and the spaced form `2 min` (valid per systemd.time(7)) must reach the parser intact rather than truncating to `2`. docs/ and .ai-dev/ are deliberately NOT swept — BUGLOG quotes the historical bad values as the defects it records. Plus: RuntimeWatchdogSec=15s and RebootWatchdogSec=0 in every copy that carries the values literally; no active ShutdownWatchdogSec= (deprecated pre-v243 alias); the firstboot-overlay copy byte-identical to the policy home; and 01-system.sh installing the drop-in from $ETC_REPO with no inline heredoc (it used to ship its own competing 10s/4min values to the same path). Plus the second mechanism of the same defect class, invisible to the directive pins: direct sysfs writes to /sys/class/watchdog/*/timeout (the feeder etc/sa02m-watchdog-feed.sh and its heredoc twin in tools/imaging/ssh-flash-safe.sh used to `echo 30 >` it against a 16s driver, the rejection swallowed by `|| true`) must be CLAMPED — no numeric literal above the cap, and every file writing the path also reads max_timeout on an uncommented line, so a file cannot satisfy the pin by naming the clamp in prose. A FAIL means a device would get a timeout systemd or the driver rejects, or a copy silently diverged from the policy home. Non-vacuous both ways: a missing enumerated file, a dead sweep, an empty extraction, or fewer than the two expected sysfs write sites FAILS. Deliberate non-flags: `=0` disables, commented-out lines (the imaging comment-out sed idiom), and READS of the sysfs timeout (max_timeout is the clamp's input).
tools.init: bash + grep (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Static gate for the RTC time-frame convention (home: the comment block at the DS3231 load in etc/sa02m-pre-start.sh) — the battery-backed chip holds UTC, so every conversion between system time and chip time must NAME utc rather than inherit it from /etc/adjtime, a file nothing in this repo writes and that timedatectl set-local-rtc / a different base image / a restored backup can flip. The class hit twice in two releases: the pre-start read half was fixed first, then lib_rtc.sh was found still writing the chip with local `date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'` — with sa02m-rtc-sync.timer firing every 30 min and the I2C path active whenever /dev/rtc1 is absent, the clock moved one timezone per write and the skew reached system time at the next boot. Pins: every hwclock chip access carries --utc (open-world over etc/ scripts/ tools/ opt/ www/ install.sh, resolved THROUGH the variable each file binds the binary to — not one shipped call site spells `hwclock` on the invocation line, so a literal grep would pass vacuously); every write_*_i2c_datetime function builds its timestamp with date -u (swept by DEFINITION, so a new chip writer in a new file is judged); every `date -s` fed by a chip-read value carries -u; nothing switches the frame to local (set-local-rtc / adjtime LOCAL); and no chip-vs-system comparison string-compares instead of computing an epoch — hwclock --show prints LOCAL time with a +03:00 offset, and a parser dropping that offset already reported a false 3-hour skew during this very fix. Non-vacuous: a missing enumerated file, fewer than 6 resolved hwclock accesses, a known caller contributing zero, fewer than 2 I2C write functions, a write function with no extractable timestamp, or no chip-sourced `date -s` FAILS rather than passing on zero matches. Deliberate non-flags: fake-hwclock (a timestamp file, no frame — masked before matching), commented-out lines, docs/ and .ai-dev/ (CHANGELOG/BUGLOG quote the bad form as the defect they record), apply.cgi's `date -s` on the operator-supplied wall-clock value (local by contract), year-plausibility tests against a constant, and the sudoers path allow-list naming /sbin/hwclock. --localtime is NOT accepted as an explicit frame: the repo declares one convention.
tools.init: bash + grep + awk (present everywhere the project builds)

tools.checks: Functional regression for apply.cgi's /etc/network/interfaces.d foreign-stanza merge: vendor post-up/comment/hwaddress lines preserved verbatim and in order, byte-identical second save (idempotency), unchanged output for a conf with no foreign lines, malformed/duplicate-stanza fallback to backup+regeneration, the 64-line/512-byte/control-char bounds, and the sibling rule (canonical always written, legacy mirrored as allow-hotplug only while live, retired once the device is gone). The merge is Bash inside a CGI, so no other row reaches it — a silent re-break of vendor-hook preservation would otherwise pass every syntax/static gate.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-conf-merge.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the rename script's per-device udev-initialized gate (etc/sa02m-iface-canonical.sh canonicalize_pair, contract §1.0): settled-canonical immediate no-op, initialized-legacy rename, the boot-0 sequence (kernel-named eth0 that udev renames to end0 mid-wait — the 6.1-class 'board unreachable on an unattended boot' regression), absent-pair budget, both degraded-fallback branches (udev db never appears), and the failed-rename exit/admin-state discipline. Runs the SHIPPED functions against a sandboxed SYS_NET/UDEV_DB pair with an `ip` PATH shim — the systemd/udev timing it enumerates is unreachable from any other row and cannot be forced on a healthy bench board.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-canonical-gate.sh

tools.checks: Regression for the installer's on-disk migration to canonical interface names (scripts/02-network.sh migrate_iface_conf): the three gate branches (canonical device live / explicit --ip protected / DUAL-CONF deferred), DUAL-CONF re-run idempotency incl. the canonical header NOT being demoted to allow-hotplug, a stanza-free legacy conf being dropped rather than copied over the live one, and eth1's allow-hotplug convention. This code only runs on a device as root during an install and its failure mode is 'the board comes up with no address' (the 1.0.3.38 Cannot-find-device class), so it gets a bench-runnable net.
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-migration.sh

tools.checks: Functional regression for the installer's gateway/DNS repair (scripts/02-network.sh ensure_gw_dns + the subnet helpers it uses from scripts/lib.sh): the mandatory subnet guard (an out-of-subnet candidate is NOT written — writing one makes the next ifup fail, networking.service FAILED, board unreachable: the 1.0.3.38 class through a new door), including via a CIDR `address a.b.c.d/NN` prefix and against a duplicated address/netmask key (two netmask lines were the one construction that got past the guard); fail-closed on any unparseable stanza with each branch asserted on its WARN TEXT, not just on 'nothing was written' (the install log is this code's only failure surface, so a message contradicting the file is itself the defect); add-only-when-absent (a present or deliberately commented-out gateway/dns-nameservers is never modified); no write into a dhcp or duplicate stanza; byte-identical re-runs with no backup churn; the .sa02m-gwbak name never clobbering the panel's .sa02m-bak restore point; insertion matching the stanza's own indent (four spaces / column 0 / TAB) without reordering hwaddress, post-up, comments or a preceding no-auto-down; and the write-failure contract — with mktemp/cp/mv stubbed to fail, and with a replace that lands the wrong content, the repair must log no OK, set no live-route flag, and leave or restore the conf (a false success would drive `ip route replace` plus a resolvconf head naming a gateway absent from the conf). Also covers sa02m_write_resolvconf_head: our stale head removed and logged, a foreign head never touched. The defect class is parsing and idempotency against real-world formatting variance, which a static grep gate cannot see — same reason iface-conf-merge and iface-migration exist. Non-vacuous: a failed or over-wide extraction, an un-retargeted conf path (which would edit the real /etc), a missing safety token in the extracted body, a missing lib.sh helper, or a fixture that stopped matching FAILS rather than passing on zero matches; the injection cases carry their own control assertion.

tools.checks: Functional RED/GREEN regression for the boot-time DNS guarantee (usr/local/sbin/sa02m-dns-ensure.sh + sa02m-wait-carrier.sh; contract docs/contracts/boot-network-dns.md). The defect it pins is SILENT: an ifup that dies on the gateway step because the PHY carrier arrived late aborts BEFORE its if-up.d stage, so /etc/network/if-up.d/000resolvconf never runs and /etc/resolv.conf stays EMPTY while address and default route look healthy — the board pings and serves its panel, and nothing fails until a name must resolve, then the OTA web update dies with 'Could not resolve host'. Covers rung 1 (an existing record is never clobbered so a real ifup always wins; a conf with no dns-nameservers writes nothing — the dhcp/2-eth case; multi-nameserver order; a KLogic-shaped conf with no-auto-down, TAB indent, comments and post-up; CRLF delivery; a control-char token, an oversized line and an invalid/leading-zero-octet token never reaching resolvconf; dns-search/dns-domain), rung 2 (empty resolv.conf regenerates from resolv.conf.d/base, a populated one is left alone, no needless fire after a rung-1 write), idempotency under the 30 s net-watchdog cadence (three runs = one write, one log line), degradation (resolvconf absent = silent no-op exit 0; a failing resolvconf -a logged and still exit 0), and the carrier wait (returns at once on carrier; TERMINATES at the budget with rc=0; IFUP_CARRIER_WAIT_SECS=0 disables it entirely; an admin-DOWN device is raised first because the kernel refuses a carrier read otherwise — without it the wait burns the whole budget every boot; --auto selects only auto+static+gateway ifaces; a malformed interface name is refused before it reaches a path or ip(8); lo is skipped; the hard 120 s ceiling stays well under ifup@'s 5-min TimeoutStartUSec, asserted so a future budget bump cannot silently cross it; and the clamp's EFFECT asserted by calling the extracted read_budget directly — the two in-situ clamp cases can only see the log line, so a clamp that logged and then returned 9999 would pass them). The resolvconf-absent guard is pinned with a LIVE logger shim on the PATH: with logger absent too, a helper missing the guard falls into rung 2, fails resolvconf -u and logs nothing anyway, so the case would pass on broken code. Also pins the wiring the mechanism depends on, which is where the mechanism most nearly died: the belt unit ordering-only (After=, never Before=), both drop-ins carrying the '-' never-fail prefix, the installer provisioning both helpers and both drop-in dirs and enabling the belt WITHOUT start, both recovery-ladder call sites, and — the OTA half — sa02m-dns-ensure.service present in the manifest's services.enable in BOTH generators (etc/sa02m-update-runner.sh AND scripts/pack-offline-update.py) plus the runner's enable loop keeping its `|| true`. That last one is not decoration: DST_RE only governs whether the FILE arrives, the runner enables only what services.enable lists, and with the entry missing from either generator the unit lands on a field device and stays inert forever with no symptom. Each half is pinned independently (removing the entry from one generator alone FAILS), and BOTH generator files are in this row's `covers` so editing either one triggers the ratchet written to protect it. Also covers the one-time OTA bootstrap shim in sa02m-eth-coldboot.sh, which exists because the ONLINE update generates its manifest from the runner already installed on the device and re-execs that same old binary before deploying — so a board coming from a pre-1.0.6.6 runner receives the belt unit DEPLOYED BUT DISABLED and the new enable list only bites on the next update: the shipped dns_ensure_bootstrap is extracted and run against a scripted systemctl shim for no-unit-file, first-pass-enables-and-marks, one-time (a later boot never re-enables, so an operator's disable stays), enabled/static/masked/unknown all left alone, and a FAILING enable still returning 0 with the marker written (no retry storm on the boot path); the harness also FAILS if the shim is never called from the script body. Plus SHELL-DIALECT coverage, added because a `: >` redirection to a marker file shipped and survived every earlier neuter: `:` is a POSIX SPECIAL built-in, so under dash (the board's /bin/sh) a redirection error on one ABORTS the script and neither 2>/dev/null nor || true catches it, while bash simply continues — a bash-only harness is blind to the whole class. Two layers: a static scan of every shipped #!/bin/sh script for a special built-in taking a redirection (runs on every host; non-vacuous — it FAILS if it did not see all three files, if a file stopped being #!/bin/sh, or if its own regex stops detecting a known-bad fixture), and a real run of the shim under a strict POSIX shell with the marker's parent impossible to create, asserting the script runs to completion. `sh` is NOT assumed to be POSIX: a `sh` that reports BASH_VERSION is rejected and the layer states it skipped, because on some dev hosts /usr/bin/sh IS bash. Method: the SHIPPED helpers are copied and sed-retargeted into a sandbox (no env seam in production code) with recording resolvconf/logger/ip shims — no root, no device, no systemd. Non-vacuous: a failed or over-wide retarget, a leftover real /etc root, a missing file, a fixture that stopped matching, or a shim never invoked FAILS rather than passing on zero matches; DNS_ENSURE_SRC / WAIT_CARRIER_SRC re-run it against a neutered helper (RED battery in the test header).
tools.init: bash (stdlib only, no deps) — run on demand: bash scripts/dev/test-iface-dns-ensure.sh

tools.checks: The image-identity reset of the Alice controller enrollment (contract docs/contracts/image-identity-reset.md). The defect class is CROSS-TENANT and silent: the gateway identifies a controller by its mTLS DN alone, so an image captured from a LINKED donor makes every clone the SAME controller as the donor — a customer's board surfacing in someone else's «Дом с Алисой», with the donor's device document (uuid4 binding ids) cloned along. The cloud agent had this exact defect and was fixed 2026-07-31 at four sites; this row gates the Alice twin, site for site. Part A — static pins: all four sites carry wipe_alice_enrollment (fewer than four FAILS) AND each one actually CALLS it — a defined-but-never-invoked wipe is inert, and the receivers are the only defence for a pre-fix stick, so the call is pinned per site in command position (the stream call pinned INSIDE prepare_clone_ids, which is also what makes the donor-side wipe follow --no-id-reset; the receivers' enclosing apply_firstboot_wiring pinned as invoked one level up); each site's path set EQUALS the contract set for its form, so both an under-wipe and a DEAD line are caught (the offline sites must NOT carry the /run row — tmpfs never reaches the image); the over-wipe tripwire (ca.crt.pem — the SHARED gateway CA — in no removal set, no rm -rf on the state tree, and the patch site keeps its CA-survived die); the sidecar dimension — the clear-lists cover the ATOMIC-WRITE leftovers by SHAPE (/var/lib/sa02m-alice/*.tmp and /etc/sa02m-alice/.alice-*), because api.py writes '<path>.tmp' then os.replace()s it and config_store leaves a mkstemp beside the conf, so a crash mid-link strands device.key.pem.tmp — THE PRIVATE KEY under a name one character off any literal list — and every such glob is EXPANDED FOR REAL against a seeded dir to prove it cannot reach ca.crt.pem (widening it to * or *.pem* FAILS); the patch site's wipe AND assertion unconditional (nesting depth 0, computed with quotes/comments masked so a one-line `if …; fi` cannot skew it) and neither swallowed by `|| true` at the call NOR warning instead of dying inside — a security clear must not be skippable by --no-id-reset, which governs the DONOR, not the artifact; the under-scope tripwire (/var/lib/sa02m-alice is STILL in cleanup-donor.sh's DENY lists — loosening a glob-collector safety list to delete one file is the obvious WRONG fix); the factory-reset floor (preserve.list still carries the cert triplet and the runner still asserts it — capture and factory reset are OPPOSITE policies and this change must not unify them); every systemctl in the on-device wipes timeout-bounded (an unbounded stop on a wedged unit hangs the capture BEFORE dd); and cloud parity across all five cloud-wipe sites. Part B — behavioural: the SHIPPED wipe of every site is extracted and run against a sandboxed fake rootfs seeded as a linked donor (both conf layouts, a populated document with uuid4 ids AND the `id: d1` / «Lab Switch» leftover the 2026-08-27 golden-image audit actually found, client_enabled = true, the cert triplet, the unit wants-link), with a recording systemctl shim for the on-device sites. Asserts cert/key/pending_claim gone; ca.crt.pem present and BYTE-IDENTICAL (the mirrored risk — no test of a deletion feature would otherwise catch an over-wipe that silently breaks every clone's client); both documents reset to the empty shape and still json-parseable; client_enabled false in both layouts with mqtt_port/log_level untouched; server.conf byte-identical; the unit disabled; stop+disable recorded; idempotent (a second run is a byte-identical no-op); and the degraded case — a rootfs with NO Alice files at all exits 0 and creates nothing, which is the `set -euo pipefail` trap an unguarded sed -i would turn into a capture aborted mid-stream BEFORE dd. Part B2 runs the shipped assertion itself: it passes a wiped image and DIES on an unwiped one, per dimension (key / document / client_enabled / unit symlink / a .tmp key sidecar / a .alice-* conf sidecar). That assertion is a WHITELIST over the identity dir — only ca.crt.pem may remain — because a blacklist of the three known names passed an image holding device.key.pem.tmp, i.e. the exact exposure this branch closes (review F1); the whitelist also fails closed on a sidecar shape nobody has invented yet, and reconstructing the pre-fix literal-name assertion turns this row RED. Non-vacuous: a failed extraction, a vacuous path set, a failed sandbox retarget, or fewer than five sidecar globs FAILS rather than passing on zero matches. Proven RED by 17 mutations (pre-fix stream and patch revisions; ca.crt.pem added to a removal set; the patch site moved under a flag; its assertion neutered with || true; timeout dropped; the DENY list loosened; a dead /run line offline; the document reset dropped; the client_enabled force dropped; the preserve.list floor broken; the CALL deleted at each of the four sites in turn; a *.tmp row dropped; a .alice-* row dropped; a sidecar glob widened to * and to *.pem*; the pre-fix blacklist assertion restored). Every site is overridable via <NAME>_SRC to re-run the battery — recipe in the test header.

tools.checks: The controller's own MQTT device id (1.0.6.22), whose whole defect class is SILENT: the telemetry service derived its id by gluing the hostname behind a fixed prefix while every other consumer named the board directly, so it published and subscribed on a subtree nobody else used — no syntax error, no dead unit, the board's own beeper/DO/alarm-LED commands simply never received, and a stale retained value making the app show the opposite of the hardware (i2cget -y 2 0x41 0x01 = 0xfd while MQTT claimed on). THIS ROW PINS EXACTLY THREE THINGS; the behavioural half lives in opt/sa02m-modbus-mqtt/tests/test_telemetry_device_id.py (row py-unit, same beat) and the split is stated here so nobody trusts this row for what it does not check. (A) No legacy id literal survives in the tracked tree: three NARROW patterns (the frozen ids; the /devices/ topic form in any placeholder shape; the prose form stating the id IS the glued hostname), swept over every tracked file, the only exclusions being files whose job is recording history verbatim (CHANGELOG.md, docs/bugs/BUGLOG.md, .ai-dev/) and the topic canon's own migration subsection. Deliberate non-flags, each verified present in this tree: /devices/sa02m-bridge (the real bridge status device), sa02m-<serial> (the CLOUD ENROLLMENT id, a different namespace keyed on the cpuinfo serial), sa02m-${STAMP} (image filenames). (B) The two INDEPENDENT id derivations — sa02m_telemetry.py and opt/sa02m-alice/sa02m_alice/config/topics.py, packages that cannot import each other at runtime — are extracted and RUN over a 9-case matrix and must agree on every case; the picker's REAL output must carry the derived id, stay non-empty and offer no legacy-prefixed controller topic. Without B the conscious duplication in topics.py is a silent-drift seam of the kind that produced the ghost binding: a frozen literal there let «Пищалка контроллера» be bound to a topic no board ever served. (C) Structure inside the owning function. Every pin here reads the body of the function that must carry the guard; the row contains NO whole-file grep, because a whole-file mention is how a gutted guard stays green — proven four times on this row alone (a cap comparison deleted with its constant left defined; an ownership proof gutted with its WARN text still naming the marker; _broker_is_loopback whose own NAME satisfied its pattern while the body became `return True`; and the order pin below, whose first-match lookup was defeated by commenting the real call out). Pinned: run() logs the live id, calls the clear, and calls init_hw() BEFORE it in CODE with comments stripped (ordering the clear first stretched the window in which a beeper/DO command is accepted-and-dropped from <1 s to 6-14 s — review finding B1); _make_hw_cb logs the drop; the clear applies the loopback gate, _broker_is_loopback really resolves the address, the ownership proof compares the retained meta/driver against TELEMETRY_DRIVER, the retained-only filter, and the collection cap. NOT pinned here, by design — tests/test_telemetry_device_id.py covers them behaviourally: the once-per-process guard, the telemetry-side allow-list, the resolution precedence, the shipped client_id truncation, and the published driver marker. The run() ORDER is pinned in BOTH places: it is the guard this branch exists to install, so it does not rest on one static check. Non-vacuous both ways: a dead sweep (<500 files), a failed import or extraction, a matrix collapsed below 3 distinct ids, a stale exclusion, a pattern that stops matching its known-bad fixture, or one widened onto a known-good look-alike all FAIL. Proven RED by 32 builder mutations over three rounds plus 7 reviewer mutations, with an expect-GREEN control proving the order pin does not cry wolf on an inline comment. Seven of those exposed hollow ratchets (four in these pins, three in the tests) and all seven were fixed, not documented away. No `covers` ON PURPOSE: the sweep is tree-wide, so a path list would let a reintroduced literal in an unlisted file skip the gate — measured 2.4 s.

tools.checks: Regression for the ES-module half of scripts/sync-app-version.py (scripts/dev/test_sync_app_version.py, stdlib unittest): a stale ?v= inside an import/export specifier (static from-imports, bare import, dynamic import(), both quote styles, multi-line bodies, an &r= suffix) is FLAGGED by --check and PATCHED by the sync; a ?v= that is not an import specifier (a runtime-built string, Array.from(...), a classic bundle) stays byte-identical; the shipped static/js tree is a byte-identical no-op; and main(['--check']) returns 1 with a stale module and 0 once synced.
